title: VendPoint Inventory Control Standard: Fill Level of a Returned Start-Up Item
content:
Inventory control standard of the VendPoint Industrial Vending Program for unused units of the item most recently added to a machine and returned into it during its start-up months: how full the item's selection already stands shapes the credit.

**Standard.** The fill level can replace the price in the standard unit credit, following the item's stock ledger against the selection's par, where the item's stock ledger is its units loaded on restock visits, less its units vended, plus its units returned to the machine and credited for vend errors, less its units withdrawn and its units billed as shrink, over all of the machine's records, and the selection's par is the par on the item's selection entry carrying the highest planogram request reference: when the ledger stands at or above the par, the price less the overstock handling charge for each unit, never below zero, replaces it; when the ledger stands at or above the near-full share of the par but below the par, the price multiplied by the near-full credit share replaces it; otherwise the price stands.

**Figures.** The overstock handling charge is 0.75 USD per unit; the near-full share of the par is 0.8 (80% of the par); the near-full credit share is 0.95.

The price is the unit price of the item's latest vend.

### Fill bands, both sides shown (hypothetical par of 20 units, so the near-full share is 16 units)

| Stock ledger | Band | Figure in place of the price, for a price of 10.00 USD |
|---|---|---|
| 21 units | At or above the par | 10.00 less 0.75: 9.25 |
| 20 units | At or above the par | 9.25 |
| 19 units | Near-full share or above, below the par | 10.00 multiplied by 0.95: 9.50 |
| 16 units | Near-full share or above, below the par | 9.50 |
| 15 units | Below the near-full share | 10.00 |

A hypothetical price of 0.50 USD on a ledger at or above the par gives 0.50 less 0.75, held at zero.

### Reading the ledger

Every record of the item on the machine counts, whatever its date: units loaded on restock visits and units returned or credited for vend errors raise the ledger; units vended, withdrawn or billed as shrink lower it.
